holes_found.description: Cross-WIN numerical inconsistency between WIN-002 and WIN-038 on the area-weighted average of H(r). WIN-002 detail_evidence (verbatim): "the area-weighted average (proper for a disc) gives H_eff ≈ 2,140 km → 35 Hz." WIN-038 detail_evidence (verbatim): "Effective heights ranging from ~1,800 km (area-weighted) to ~5,200 km (energy-weighted) yield predicted fundamentals of 14–42 Hz." I recomputed the standard area-weighted average analytically: H_eff = (2/R^2) * integral_0^R r*H(r) dr = 2,134.8 km → 35.1 Hz using H0=8,537, L=8,619, R=20,015. WIN-002's 2,140 km/35 Hz is correct; WIN-038's 1,800 km (which drives its 42 Hz upper bound) is off by ~15% from WIN-002 and from the analytical result. A dome-defender with fresh eyes reading both WINs simultaneously will notice: "the reviewers cannot even agree on what area-weighted means for the same integral on the same H(r) — pick a lane." The 1,800 km figure appears to be an r^2 or volume-scaling weighting (my calc: r^2 weighting gives 1,676 km, close to 1,800), but it is labeled "area-weighted" — matching WIN-002's label but not its result. This is the strongest defender-pivot on the panel today.
holes_found.recommendation: Reconcile WIN-002 and WIN-038 to the same numerical result. Two options: (a) [preferred] update WIN-038 to use WIN-002's numbers — area-weighted 2,140 km → 35 Hz — and drop the 1,800 km / 42 Hz upper-bound, giving a clean 14-35 Hz range that is fully consistent with WIN-002. (b) Retain the 1,800 km figure but explicitly relabel it (e.g. "radial-density-weighted (r^2 scaling): ~1,800 km → ~42 Hz") so a defender cannot claim we contradict ourselves. Option (a) is lower-risk and rhetorically stronger (14-35 Hz is still an order-of-magnitude gap from 7.83 Hz). Whichever option is chosen, the rationale should be documented via an EXP so decider carries the intent through to any future prose-polish edits.

holes_found.description: Numerical rounding error in paragraph 1 of WIN-038 detail_evidence: "at r = 10,000 km, f ≈ 27 Hz." Recomputed: H(10,000) = 8,537 * exp(-10,000/8,619) = 2,675.6 km; f = 299,792/(4*2,675.6) = 28.01 Hz. The stated 27 Hz is rounded down by 1 Hz (3.6% error); the correct rounding is 28 Hz. Neighboring values are correctly rounded (r=5,960 → 17.53 Hz stated as 17.5 Hz; r=20,015 → 89.5 Hz stated as ~90 Hz), so 27 stands out as an inconsistent rounding-down. Not a verdict-impacting error but a fresh-eyes reader running the numbers along with us will catch it.

advocate_mode.best_defense: A dome-defender operating with our stated methodological principles could construct the following: "You (the reviewer) are treating H(r) = 8,537 * exp(-r/8,619) as a fixed physical constraint of the model, but it is a first-order phenomenological *parameterization* fit to gravitational data — not a derived structural equation. If Schumann resonance observations require H_max >= 9,572 km at the pole, the honest correction is to update the H(r) fit to accommodate the observation. A 12% upward adjustment at r=0 changes almost nothing about the model's other predictions — the disc-radius, sun-altitude, and moon-altitude parameters are not derived from H(r); they are independent. The dome model already treats H(r) as approximate (the exponential fit itself is an ansatz). The pole-floor argument works only against the current parameterization; the model as a *class* survives with an updated exponent."
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: The current text closes this at the consequence level: paragraph 4(i) states that quarter-wave retreat requires "simultaneously withdraw WIN-029 and delete the 9,572 km firmament-height figure propagated throughout the model." The implicit closure is that H(r) is not free-standing — it underwrites multiple sibling WINs, most obviously WIN-029's 5.3% "confirmation." A rated-3 upgrade is available but optional: add a one-sentence footnote naming which other WINs depend on H(r) (WIN-002 uses it, WIN-029 back-derives against it, WIN-034 cross-references it, the rim value of 837 km underwrites disc-cavity geometry claims throughout Part 2), so a defender who says "just update H(r)" is confronted with the cascade rather than trusting an implicit "propagated throughout the model" claim. Given the current text already carries the closure implicitly, this remains a rated-2 defense — noteworthy for future polish but not urgent.

deeper_analysis:
WIN-038 at c10 is a mature, load-bearing panel — nine prior cycles of adversarial review have hardened it substantially, and the EXP-394 batch on 2026-05-16 closed the four most consequential c9 minor holes. The verdict (Self-Contradicted) is safe. Fresh-eyes attention this cycle focused on quantitative recomputation and cross-WIN consistency because prior cycles had been re-verifying prose patches — an opportunity for arithmetic errors to accumulate unnoticed. That paid off: two new findings surfaced that no prior cycle caught, both arithmetic.

Thinking about the other side: a dome-defender confronted with a 9-cycle-reviewed WIN panel is looking for cracks in the numerical foundation, not in the prose framing. The most damaging finding a defender could surface is exactly the cross-WIN arithmetic inconsistency I flagged: WIN-002 and WIN-038 both attack the same H(r) integral and give different area-weighted numerical results. "Which is it, 1,800 km or 2,140 km? You cannot both be right." This does not overturn the verdict — even 1,800 km gives 42 Hz which is nowhere near 7.83 Hz — but it undermines the rhetorical claim that our numbers are careful. A defender writing an AI-adversarial rebuttal would open with this cross-WIN mismatch and use it to seed doubt about the entire pole-floor arithmetic.

The counter-argument I find persuasive: the current text state is actually the *safer* state before the discrepancy is exposed. The moderate finding is discovered by us, in-house, at c10, and can be fixed via a narrow decider self-apply before a defender ever finds it. The cost of the fix is one prose edit (either replace 1,800 with 2,140 or explicitly relabel 1,800 as "r^2 weighting"); the benefit is closing an in-panel arithmetic vulnerability that has been sitting there for at least 51 days (since the EXP-394 landing) and possibly since the WIN was first written. This is exactly the kind of finding spot-checks are for.

On the minor 27→28 Hz rounding: this is a genuine arithmetic error, not a rhetorical device. It has been sitting in the text through nine review cycles and none of them caught it, because none of them independently ran the H(r) numbers at r=10,000. This is a good case study for why Lens C (quantitative verification) matters even on well-reviewed panels — the accumulated review cycles were all prose-attack cycles, not arithmetic-recomputation cycles. One clean numerical sweep surfaces two errors that nine adversarial-prose passes missed.

Advocate mode found one rated-2 defense ("just update H(r)") that the text closes implicitly but not explicitly. Adding a named-cascade footnote would upgrade this to rated-1 (fully neutralized) at the cost of one sentence. This is a good future EXP target if the operator wants belt-and-braces on the paragraph-4(i) argument. It is not urgent — the current implicit closure is defensible if a defender presses.

Cross-WIN consistency: the WIN-002 / WIN-029 / WIN-038 triple is the internal triple-count backbone of Part 2 Schumann coverage. WIN-002 and WIN-029 both share the Self-Contradicted verdict with WIN-038 and are argumentatively consistent at the verdict level. The two inconsistencies (area-weighted number, Sentman year) are both narrow and both fixable.

Recommended action minor_edit rather than no_change because two findings — the WIN-002/WIN-038 area-weighted mismatch (moderate) and the 27→28 Hz rounding (minor) — call for a narrow decider self-apply. Neither touches the verdict; both close in-panel arithmetic vulnerabilities before a defender can weaponize them. The carry-over c9 minor holes (globe-fingerprint phrasing, Collin chapter, paragraph density) remain deferred per prior recommendations.
